newsitem.title: USA: Egghead to close stores, restructure, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Egghead to close stores, restructure, take charge.

text.p: Computer software retailer Egghead Inc. said Friday it plans to close 77 stores, or nearly half the total, and take a $30 million charge as part of a broad restructuring.

In a statement, Egghead, which sells computer software, hardware and accessories, also said Chief Executive Officer Terry Strom and senior vice presidents Kurt Conklin and Ron Smith will step down after a transitional period. Chairman George Orban will replace Strom, who will continue to work with Egghead as a consultant.
The company said it was closing 77 of its 156 Egghead stores and reducing the number of markets in which it competes to 24 markets from 54.
Egghead is also cutting its headquarters staff, closing its Lancaster, Pa., distribution centre and offering its headquarters building in Spokane, Wash., and other real estate for sale.
Egghead said the charge, to be taken in its fiscal fourth quarter ending March 29, will cover costs and write-offs related to closed stores, inventory liquidation, severance and the asset sales.
The company said the reorganization was expected to cut headquarters and distribution expense by almost $20 million a year and sharply reduce its operating loss in the next fiscal year.

"Our objective this coming fiscal year is to reduce our operating losses, improve our business processes and devote our resources to creating a foundation for renewed growth," Orban said. "The actions approved by the board amount to a remaking of Egghead in a way that we believe should give us the opportunity to turn the company around."

For the third quarter ended in December, Egghead earned $1.5 million, or 9 cents a share, compared with a loss of $941,000, or 5 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter. Sales fell to $113.2 million from $121.7 million.

For the nine months, the company had a net loss of $3.7 million, or 21 cents a share, vs. a loss of $7.6 million, or 44 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales fell to $271.8 million from $307 million.

Revenues for the nine months from the 79 remaining Egghead stores accounted for $164.7 million or 64 percent of Egghead's fiscal year-to-date retail store revenue. Comparable store revenues for the remaining group of stores fell 4 percent for the nine-month period.

Egghead said it plans to replace some original Egghead stores with larger stores emphasising broader merchandise assortments, computer upgrades and installation services. The company also expects to add 15 new larger stores by the end of fiscal 1998.
The company also plans to invest in its Internet business.
"This business is in its infancy, but is showing promising growth and consumer acceptance," Orban said.
In November, Egghead became the first major computer products retailer to deliver programmes over the Internet directly to customers' computers.
